clinical_knowledge.topic: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes recommending dietary modifications (low-FODMAP diet) and stress reduction, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: alternating diarrhea and constipation with abdominal cramping for 6 months

Key HPI features: A 29-year-old male presents to the clinic with alternating diarrhea and constipation with abdominal cramping for 6 months. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Inflammatory bowel disease without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: rectal bleeding or blood in the stool, unintentional weight loss, or nocturnal symptoms that wake the patient from sleep.
management_principles: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 29-year-old male presents with a 6-month history of alternating diarrhoea and constipation with abdominal cramping, no red-flag features on screening.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), mixed bowel habit subtype. DDx: inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease, colorectal cancer.
reference_soap.plan: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Implement evidence-based management plan: Recommend dietary modifications (Low-FODMAP diet), stress reduction

teaching.one_liner: A functional gut disorder where stress and certain foods trigger cramping and alternating bowel habits, without any structural disease on testing.
red_flags: Rectal bleeding or blood in the stool — atypical for IBS and warrants investigation for IBD or malignancy
Unintentional weight loss — raises concern for organic pathology rather than a functional disorder
Nocturnal symptoms that wake the patient from sleep — not typical of IBS and suggest an organic cause

must_ask.say: Do you swing between diarrhoea and constipation, or is it just one or the other?
Does the cramping ease once you've had a bowel movement?
Do your symptoms flare up more when you're stressed?
Are there any foods that seem to set it off?
Have you ever noticed blood in your stool?
Have you lost any weight without trying to?
